questions.stem: The 'Cabinet Mission' of 1946 arrived in India to discuss the transfer of power. Who among the following was NOT a member of this mission?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Cabinet Mission (1946) consisted of three British cabinet ministers: Lord Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State for India), Sir Stafford Cripps (President of the Board of Trade), and A.V. Alexander (First Lord of the Admiralty). Lord Mountbatten was not a member; he arrived later in 1947 as the final Viceroy.
DECOY BUSTING: Cripps had previously led the failed Cripps Mission in 1942. 
EXAM INSIGHT: The Cabinet Mission famously rejected the Muslim League's demand for a separate, sovereign state of Pakistan, instead proposing a weak Centre with grouped provinces.

questions.stem: Which prominent leader of the Indian National Movement famously declared, 'Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it'?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, one of the famous 'Lal-Bal-Pal' triumvirate of extremist leaders, made this roaring declaration in 1916. He strongly opposed the moderate faction's policy of 'pray, petition, and protest', demanding outright self-rule (Swaraj).
DECOY BUSTING: Lala Lajpat Rai (Punjab Kesari) died after a lathi charge protesting the Simon Commission. Bipin Chandra Pal was the third of the trio. Gandhi advocated non-violent Satyagraha.
EXAM INSIGHT: Tilak also started two famous newspapers to spread nationalist ideas: the 'Kesari' (in Marathi) and the 'Mahratta' (in English).
